children.translated_text: Praiseworthy are those drops of spray from the flowing stream of the nectar of faith of those who partake of special devotion to the <s>Jina</s> (Victor),

children.text: niścetano 'py ucitacetanatām ivaiti yaḥ pūjyapūjanavidhau kusumādivargaḥ // KAvk_93.1 //
children.translated_text: by which even the lifeless group of flowers and such seems to attain a fitting consciousness in the ritual of worshipping the Venerable One. // KAvk_93.1 //
In <s>Śrāvastī</s>, as the <s>Jina</s> sat in solitude in <s>Jetavana</s> long ago,
<s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> approached and addressed the Blessed One: // KAvk_93.2 //
'Like devotion to you, renowned everywhere for great and precious qualities,

children.text: bhagavan prauḍhim āyātā kanyā mama sumāgadhā // KAvk_93.3 //
children.translated_text: O Blessed One, my daughter <s>Sumāgadhā</s> has come to the fullness of maturity. // KAvk_93.3 //
Of the illustrious caravan-leader, in the city of <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>,
a son named <s>Vṛṣabhadatta</s> is desired as the recipient of her hand. // KAvk_93.4 //

children.text: kanyāṃ dadāmi tāṃ tasmai bhagavan yadi manyase /
children.translated_text: I shall give that daughter to him, O Blessed One, if you approve,
for my wealth and life depend on you; I take refuge in your command.' // KAvk_93.5 //
When this was said by him, the Blessed One, pure-hearted with paternal affection,

children.text: ko doṣas tanayā tasmai dīyatām ity abhāṣata // KAvk_93.6 //
children.translated_text: said: 'What fault is there? Let your daughter be given to him.' // KAvk_93.6 //

children.text: śāstuḥ śāsanam ādāya sādaraṃ pranipatya tam /
children.translated_text: Having received the Teacher's instruction, and reverently prostrating before him,
the illustrious <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> departed to his own mansion. // KAvk_93.7 //
Then he gave his daughter <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, with surpassing wealth,

children.text: arhāyaṃ sa dadau tasmai bhūriratnāmbarapradaḥ // KAvk_93.8 //
children.translated_text: to that worthy one, bestowing abundant jewels and garments. // KAvk_93.8 //

children.text: dattā dūrataraṃ deśam atha yāntī sumāgadhā /
children.translated_text: Having been given away, as <s>Sumāgadhā</s> was departing to a distant land,
her eyes became tearful from the memory of the Blessed One's feet. // KAvk_93.9 //
After a long time, having reached the city of <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>,
devoted to the service of her husband, she always lived in her husband's house. // KAvk_93.10 //
Once, her mother-in-law, who was engaged in preparing food offerings,
named <s>Dhanavatī</s>, devoted to immeasurable expenditure, said to her: // KAvk_93.11 //
'Prepare all the articles of worship ready, O <s>Sumāgadhā</s>!

children.text: gṛhān naḥ prātar āgantā jagatpūjyaguṇo jinaḥ // KAvk_93.12 //
children.translated_text: Tomorrow morning the <s>Jina</s>, worshipped by the world for his qualities, will come to our house. // KAvk_93.12 //
The venerable ones, the seat of reverence, worthy of worship by all people—
the <s>kṣapaṇakas</s> (Jain ascetics), devoted to destroying delusion, will assemble.' // KAvk_93.13 //

children.text: ity uktā sā tayā tatra babhūvārambhatatparā /
children.translated_text: Thus told by her, she became earnestly devoted to the preparations there,

children.text: jñātvā bhikṣugaṇāyeva tāṃ pūjāṃ parikalpitām // KAvk_93.14 //
children.translated_text: knowing that the worship had been arranged for a group of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). // KAvk_93.14 //
Then on the next day, naked <s>kṣapaṇakas</s> (Jain ascetics) entered the house,
with plucked-out hair and beards, sharpened in their vows through mortification. // KAvk_93.15 //
Seeing those shameless, unclothed ones, <s>Sumāgadhā</s> [regarded them]
like buffaloes fattened by habitual feeding on beans and grass. // KAvk_93.16 //
Ashamed, covering her face with her garment in the presence of her elders,
bowed down with grief and disillusionment, she addressed her mother-in-law: // KAvk_93.17 //
'Alas! This is indeed a custom long observed—

children.text: digambarāṇām apy agre yad ihāste vadhūjanaḥ // KAvk_93.18 //
children.translated_text: that a young bride should sit before these naked ones! // KAvk_93.18 //
These untamed ones eat in your house without horns;

children.text: amānuṣatvān naiteṣāṃ lajjante nūnam aṅganāḥ // KAvk_93.19 //
children.translated_text: since they are not human, surely women do not feel shame before them. // KAvk_93.19 //

children.text: asthāne bhavatāṃ bhaktiḥ ko 'yam ucchṛṅkhalaḥ kramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Your devotion is misplaced! What is this licentious custom?

children.text: na tyaktam aśanaṃ yena sa kathaṃ vastram ujjhati // KAvk_93.20 //
children.translated_text: One who has not renounced food — how does he renounce clothing? // KAvk_93.20 //
By the very act of tearing out hair, their pitilessness has been demonstrated;
by renouncing even a loincloth, what talk can there be of moral conduct among decent people?

children.text: dambhārambhabhayaṃkare ca vadane krodhaḥ svayaṃ lakṣyate
children.translated_text: On their faces, terrifying with the onset of deceit, anger itself is visible—

children.text: nagnānām aśanaiṣiṇāṃ niyaminām eṣāṃ paśūnām iva // KAvk_93.21 //
children.translated_text: of these naked food-seekers, so-called self-controlled ones, who are like animals. // KAvk_93.21 //

children.text: yatraite paśavaḥ pūjyās tatrotsāryā bhavanti ke /
children.translated_text: Where these animals are worshipped, who then can be cast out?
Or rather, this is a fault of the region — a custom of blind followers.' // KAvk_93.22 //

children.text: iti bruvāṇāṃ tāṃ śvaśrūr viṣaṇṇā pratyabhāṣata /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, her mother-in-law, dejected, replied to her:

children.text: pitus te bhavane bhadre pūjyate vada kīdṛśaḥ // KAvk_93.23 //
children.translated_text: 'Tell me, dear one, in your father's house, what kind [of person] is worshipped?' // KAvk_93.23 //

children.text: sāvadan matpitur gehe pūjyate bhagavān jinaḥ /
children.translated_text: She said: 'In my father's house, the Blessed <s>Jina</s> is worshipped,
who out of compassion for all beings is devoted to the utmost welfare. // KAvk_93.24 //
Absorbed in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), with serene eyes, an ocean of perfect beauty,
bearing a broad and straight bridge of a nose,
radiant with the charm of ornament-free yet luminous earlobes—

children.text: kāntyaivāsau kim api viduṣāṃ śāntim antas tanoti // KAvk_93.25 //
children.translated_text: by his splendor alone he instills an ineffable inner peace in the wise. // KAvk_93.25 //
Upon his head he bears a jewel made of innate, abundant, overflowing light,
his arms like the trunk of a lordly elephant, golden in luster,
on his palms the auspicious lines of conch, banner, lotus, and garland—
he bears the marks worthy of the great sovereignty of tranquility. // KAvk_93.26 //
His nature, which inspires longing in the great sages, is free from all calculations of desire;

children.text: niḥśeṣitasmṛtibhuvaḥ pramadāśrayasya rāgojjhitasya sutarām adharaḥ sarāgaḥ // KAvk_93.27 //
children.translated_text: though dwelling in the abode of beautiful women who obliterate all recollection, he is utterly free from passion — yet his lower lip appears reddened. // KAvk_93.27 //
His form delights in intimate communion; his <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) reclines within the heart;

children.text: kṣāntis tanmayakāriṇī hṛdi dayā gāḍhaṃ samāśleṣiṇī /
children.translated_text: his <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) makes one absorbed in it; his <s>dayā</s> (compassion) firmly embraces the heart.
Of that one who adorns all hopes and is attached to his many beloved devotees,
that unprecedented jewel's incomparable majesty is discerned — tranquility pregnant with detachment. // KAvk_93.28 //

children.text: pūjyaḥ sa bhavane 'smākaṃ yasya pravrajyayā satām /
children.translated_text: He is worshipped in our house — he by whose renunciation
the minds of the good bear the transparency of garments of <s>śīla</s> (moral virtue). // KAvk_93.29 //
That jewel of universal protection — by merely remembering him,

children.text: rāgadveṣogradaṃṣṭreṇa bādhyate na punar janaḥ // KAvk_93.30 //
children.translated_text: people are no longer afflicted by the terrible fangs of passion and hatred, the serpent of worldly existence.' // KAvk_93.30 //

children.text: iti tasyā vacaḥ śvaśrūḥ śrutvā śrotrarasāyanam /
children.translated_text: Having heard her words, which were nectar for the ears, the mother-in-law,

children.text: sadyaḥ prasādaviśadā tāṃ jagāda pramodinī // KAvk_93.31 //
children.translated_text: instantly purified by faith, spoke to her joyfully: // KAvk_93.31 //
'Is there any means of seeing him, O beautiful one?

children.text: api tvatpuṇyasaṃbandhād vayam apy amṛtāspadam // KAvk_93.32 //
children.translated_text: Through connection with your merit, might we too [reach] the abode of immortality?' // KAvk_93.32 //
Thus lovingly entreated by her mother-in-law, she, attentive and respectful in mind,

children.text: taṃ vaḥ saṃdarśayāmīti babhāṣe bhaktimāninī // KAvk_93.33 //
children.translated_text: said: 'I shall show him to you' — she who was proud of her devotion. // KAvk_93.33 //
Wishing to carry through the burden of her great vow's fulfillment,
she, poised on the balance of doubt, became absorbed in meditation for a moment. // KAvk_93.34 //
Then, having ascended to the upper story of the palace, in the direction frequented by the Blessed One,
she prostrated and released a handful of flowers worthy of worshipping the Venerable One. // KAvk_93.35 //
Having performed worship with flowers, incense, and water, with face turned toward his feet,
she spoke with wide eyes choked with tears of joy: // KAvk_93.36 //
'I am indeed pitiable, O Blessed One, deprived of the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels);

children.text: tavāśramamṛgīvāhaṃ dūraṃ deśam imam gatā // KAvk_93.37 //
children.translated_text: like a deer of your hermitage, I have gone to this distant land. // KAvk_93.37 //

children.text: tvatpādapadmayugalaṃ śaraṇam prapannāṃ dūrasthitām api dṛśā spṛśa māṃ dayālo /
children.translated_text: I have taken refuge at the pair of your lotus feet — though I stand far away, touch me with your gaze, O Compassionate One!

children.text: vātsalyapeśaladhiyāṃ mahatāṃ pravāsadurīkṛteṣu karuṇā na tanutvam eti // KAvk_93.38 //
children.translated_text: For the great ones whose minds are tender with paternal love, compassion does not diminish toward those made distant by separation. // KAvk_93.38 //
O Blessed One, I, the daughter of your servant, have invited you today;

children.text: prātar āgamanenaiva mānaṃ vitara me vibho // KAvk_93.39 //
children.translated_text: by coming tomorrow morning, bestow honor upon me, O Mighty Lord.' // KAvk_93.39 //
Having uttered thus, the variegated garland of flowers released by her,
as if alive, traveled through the sky as a messenger of devotion. // KAvk_93.40 //

children.text: sā śvetaraktaharitāsitapuṣpapālī khe dhūpadhūmaśabalā śanakaiḥ prayāntī /
children.translated_text: That garland of white, red, green, and dark flowers, dappled with the smoke of incense, slowly moving through the sky,

children.text: bālāmbudapraṇayinī suciraṃ cakāśe saṃcālicāpalatikeva śacīdhavasya // KAvk_93.41 //
children.translated_text: courting the young clouds, shone for a long time like the trembling creeper-bow of <s>Indra</s> (the rainbow). // KAvk_93.41 //
Then, reaching <s>Jetavana</s> in an instant, that garland,

children.text: sā bhaktiśālinī śāstuḥ papāta caraṇābjayoḥ // KAvk_93.42 //
children.translated_text: imbued with devotion, fell at the lotus feet of the Teacher. // KAvk_93.42 //

children.text: bhagavān api sarvajñaḥ sarvaṃ jñātvā samīhitam /
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, being omniscient, having known all that was desired

children.text: sumāgadhāyāḥ kāruṇyād ānandam avadat puraḥ // KAvk_93.43 //
children.translated_text: by <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, out of compassion spoke to <s>Ānanda</s> before [the assembly]: // KAvk_93.43 //
'We must go tomorrow morning to the city of <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s>;
<s>Sumāgadhā</s> requests the worship of me together with the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' // KAvk_93.44 //
'From here onward, it is more than one hundred and sixty <s>yojanas</s> (leagues),

children.text: ekenāhnā ca gantavyaṃ na vilambo 'tra yujyate // KAvk_93.45 //
children.translated_text: and it must be traveled in a single day — delay is not appropriate here.' // KAvk_93.45 //

children.text: vyomnā maharddhyā śaknoti gantuṃ yo yaḥ prabhāvavān /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever is powerful and able to go through the sky by great <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power)—

children.text: nimantraṇaśalākāṃ tvaṃ tasmai tasmai samarpaya // KAvk_93.46 //
children.translated_text: give the invitation-stick to each of those.' // KAvk_93.46 //
Thus directed by the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), he announced to the monks
the invitation reachable only by a single day's travel, through the invitation-sticks. // KAvk_93.47 //
When the invitation-sticks were taken by all those of great supernatural power,

children.text: pūrṇaḥ kumbhopadhānīyaḥ sthaviro 'py agrahīt kramāt // KAvk_93.48 //
children.translated_text: the elder <s>Pūrṇa Kumbhopadhānīya</s> also took one in turn. // KAvk_93.48 //
When, having arrived with such power as he had attained, the stick was extended

children.text: pāṇau prāha tam ānandaḥ kiṃcit smitasitānanaḥ // KAvk_93.49 //
children.translated_text: in his hand, <s>Ānanda</s> addressed him with a slightly smiling face: // KAvk_93.49 //
'You cannot walk even two steps to <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s house,
and one hundred and sixty <s>yojanas</s> must be crossed in half a day!' // KAvk_93.50 //
Thus addressed by him, the elder, with face cast down in embarrassment,

children.text: acintayat svavargāgre nyūnabhāvo hi duḥsahaḥ // KAvk_93.5l //
children.translated_text: reflected: 'Inferiority among one's peers is indeed unbearable.' // KAvk_93.51 //
The <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), birth, old age, and the rest, accumulated since beginningless time —

children.text: hantuṃ sapatnaiḥ śakyante prāptum ṛddhipadaṃ kiyat // KAvk_93.52 //
children.translated_text: how far can one attain the station of supernatural powers when there are enemies to be slain? // KAvk 93.52 //
As he thought thus with a mind of intense disillusionment,

children.text: prādur āsīt kṣaṇenaiva maharddhiḥ śuddhacetasaḥ // KAvk_93.53 //
children.translated_text: in an instant, great supernatural power manifested in that pure-hearted one. // KAvk 93.53 //
Then, when the night had passed, at dawn all the monks,
in various divine forms, went through the sky in celestial mansions. // KAvk 93.54 //
Meanwhile, in the house of her husband, filled with preparations for a great festival,
<s>Sumāgadhā</s>, eager for the sight of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, // KAvk 93.55 //
having ascended the palace together with her mother-in-law, father-in-law, and husband,
stood intent upon preparing offerings of flowers, incense, and honors. // KAvk 93.56 //
Then the monk <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, mounted on a horse-chariot,
wondrous with various divine powers, appeared first. // KAvk 93.57 //
Seeing him, radiant like the sun, the father-in-law and others, amazed,

children.text: ūcuḥ sumāgadhāṃ prītyā kim eṣa bhagavān iti // KAvk_93.58 //
children.translated_text: joyfully asked <s>Sumāgadhā</s>: 'Is this the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' // KAvk 93.58 //
She said: 'This is not the <s>Bhagavān</s> who is seen with the radiance of the sun;
this is the monk <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, of undiminished splendor.' // KAvk 93.59 //
As chariots arrived one after another, the father-in-law and others

children.text: kim ayaṃ kim ayaṃ bhadre bhagavān iti tāṃ jaguḥ // KAvk_93.60 //
children.translated_text: asked her: 'Is this one the <s>Bhagavān</s>? Is this one, O fair one?' // KAvk 93.60 //
She said: 'This is not the Teacher. These are monks devoted to his teaching,
praiseworthy in tranquility, blazing with the radiance of austerity.' // KAvk 93.61 //
'He who comes from afar, mounted upon a beautiful peak of a mountain adorned with lovely golden trees,

children.text: āścaryakṛn mūrta iva prabhāvaḥ śrīmān mahākāśyapa eṣa bhikṣuḥ // KAvk_93.62 //
children.translated_text: a wonder-worker, as if power incarnate — this glorious monk is <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>.' // KAvk 93.62 //
'He who comes through the sky, mounted on a lion-chariot of deep sound like a rain-cloud full of water,

children.text: vyomnā samabhyeti gunaiḥ pragītaḥ sa eṣa bhikṣur bhuvi śāriputraḥ // KAvk_93.63 //
children.translated_text: praised for his virtues — that is the monk <s>Śāriputra</s> on earth.' // KAvk 93.63 //

children.text: āruhya kailāsam ivātiśubhraṃ dvipam caturdantam anantakāntiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who approaches mounted on a four-tusked elephant, exceedingly white like <s>Kailāsa</s>, of infinite radiance,

children.text: āyāti yaḥ puṇyavatāṃ jagatsu maudgalyanāmā ca sa eṣa bhikṣuḥ // KAvk_93.64 //
children.translated_text: among the meritorious in the worlds — that monk is named <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>.' // KAvk 93.64 //
'He who approaches mounted on a golden lotus with a lapis-lazuli stalk, rich with jewel-like stamens,

children.text: upaiti yaḥ saurabhapūritāśaḥ sa eṣa bhikṣuḥ prathito 'niruddhaḥ // KAvk_93.65 //
children.translated_text: the quarters filled with fragrance — that is the renowned monk <s>Aniruddha</s>.' // KAvk 93.65 //
'He who rides a <s>Garuḍa</s> (divine eagle) at the summit of the sky, the clouds blown aside by the wind of its wings,

children.text: vigāhate sphitavanena bhikṣur maitrāyaṇīsūnur ayaṃ sa pūrṇaḥ // KAvk_93.66 //
children.translated_text: plunging through a dense forest — this monk is <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the son of <s>Maitrāyaṇī</s>.' // KAvk 93.66 //

children.text: anantam āsthāya nitāntaśāntam īrṣyāpathaṃ sattvamahodadhir yaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who rides upon something infinite and utterly peaceful — a great ocean of beings on the path free from jealousy,

children.text: prabhāmṛtaiḥ sarpati tarpitāśaḥ prabhāvavān eṣyajid eṣa bhikṣuḥ // KAvk_93.67 //
children.translated_text: who glides forth, the quarters nourished by nectarean radiance — this powerful monk is <s>Eṣyajit</s>.' // KAvk 93.67 //
'He who approaches mounted on a great golden palm tree, adorned with swaying creeper-bracelets,

children.text: yaḥ puṇyapūrṇadyutir abhyupaiti sa eṣa bhikṣur matimān upālī // KAvk_93.68 //
children.translated_text: his splendor full of merit — that is the wise monk <s>Upāli</s>.' // KAvk 93.68 //
'He who comes mounted on the peak of a lapis-lazuli celestial mansion, with leaf-designs blazing with gold and jewels,

children.text: limpann ivāgacchati yaḥ prabhābhiḥ kātyāyano nāma sa eṣa bhikṣuḥ // KAvk_93.69 //
children.translated_text: as if painting the sky with his radiance — that monk is named <s>Kātyāyana</s>.' // KAvk 93.69 //

children.text: śarīriṇaṃ dharmam ivādhiruhya vigāhate khaṃ vṛṣavāhano yaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who rides a bull, mounting as if upon the embodied <s>Dharma</s>, penetrating the sky,

children.text: pṛṣṭhaḥ pratiṣṭhāpariniṣṭhitānāṃ gariṣṭhadhīḥ kauṣṭhila eṣa bhikṣuḥ // KAvk_93.70 //
children.translated_text: foremost among those established in firm foundations, of supreme wisdom — that monk is <s>Kauṣṭhila</s>.' // KAvk 93.70 //
'He who comes, now making the sky beautiful with waves of smiles from the radiance of celestial-mansion-swans, now

children.text: kurvan samabhyeti taponidhir yaḥ pilindavatsāhvaya eṣa bhikṣuḥ // KAvk_93.7l //
children.translated_text: a storehouse of austerity — that monk is called <s>Pilindavatsa</s>.' // KAvk 93.71 //
'He who wanders and approaches in the midst of a grove with a canopy of blooming creepers —

children.text: sa śroṇakoṭiḥ śruta eṣa bhikṣur akṣuṇṇalakṣmīr gṛhanirvyapekṣaḥ // KAvk_93.72 //
children.translated_text: that is the renowned monk <s>Śroṇakoṭi</s>, of undiminished fortune, indifferent to domestic life.' // KAvk 93.72 //

children.text: yaś cakravartī divi bhāti so 'yaṃ śāstuḥ suto rāhulakābhidhānaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who shines in the sky as a universal monarch — he is the son of the Teacher, named <s>Rāhulaka</s>,
the directions adorned with golden radiance — appearing like <s>Meru</s> in another form.' // KAvk 93.73 //

children.text: ete giribhyo 'tha digantarebhyaḥ kṣmāmaṇḍalād vyomataṭāntarāc ca /
children.translated_text: 'These innumerable and wondrous assemblies of monks come from mountains, from the spaces between the directions,
from the surface of the earth, and from the expanse of the sky, seated upon various jeweled thrones and vehicles.' // KAvk 93.74 //

children.text: tayā krameṇeti nivedyamānaṃ te bhikṣusaṃghaṃ vimukhaṃ vilokya /
children.translated_text: As she described them one by one, they — looking upon the assembly of monks, though formerly averse —

children.text: yayuḥ praharṣādbhutasaṃbhramāṇāṃ vidheyatāṃ tulyam ananyalakṣmyāḥ // KAvk_93.75 //
children.translated_text: attained a state equal to that of those overwhelmed by wonder and delight, a matchless fortune. // KAvk 93.75 //
Then the world became the color of blazing golden dust, luminous as a hundred suns,
yet cool as a hundred garlands of the moon, through the cessation of all particular torments. // KAvk 93.76 //
Then, accompanied by the retinue and service offered on a vast celestial procession by the immortals led by <s>Dhanapati</s> (Kubera), <s>Śakra</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: amarapurapurastrīkīrṇapuṣpaprabhāvān nayanapatham ayāsīt puṇyabhājāṃ jinendraḥ // KAvk_93.77 //
children.translated_text: amid showers of flowers scattered by the women of the celestial city, the Lord of the Conquerors came within the range of vision of the fortunate. // KAvk 93.77 //

children.text: aṣṭādaśadvārapathā puraṃ tat sa tulyam aṣṭādaśamūrtir eva /
children.translated_text: Having entered that city of eighteen gateways — he of eighteen forms, as it were —

children.text: praviśya cakre śaśikāntaratnaśikhāmayaṃ veśma sumāgadhāyāḥ // KAvk_93.78 //
children.translated_text: he entered the house of <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, made of moonstone jewels at the pinnacle. // KAvk 93.78 //

children.text: abhyarcitas tatra bahuprakāraiḥ pūrṇopacāraiḥ praṇipatya sarvaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Honored there with many kinds of complete offerings, with all bowing in reverence,

children.text: apūjayat paurajanaḥ samantād bahiś ca bhittipratibimbitaṃ tam // KAvk_93.79 //
children.translated_text: the townspeople worshipped from the outside even his image reflected on the walls. // KAvk 93.79 //

children.text: sumāgadhāyā dayayā dayāluḥ pūjāṃ gṛhītvā bhagavān sasaṃghaḥ /
children.translated_text: The compassionate <s>Bhagavān</s>, out of kindness to <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, having received the worship together with the <s>Saṅgha</s>,
bestowed faith upon all the descendants by the distribution of gracious glances. // KAvk 93.80 //

children.text: sumāgadhā saśvaśurādivargā sahāparaiḥ paurajanaiś ca sarvāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, together with her father-in-law and others, and all the other townspeople —

children.text: śāstus tayā deśanayā babhūvuḥ śuddhāśayās tatkṣaṇadṛṣṭasatyāḥ // KAvk_93.81 //
children.translated_text: through the Teacher's discourse, at that very moment became purified in mind and saw the Truths. // KAvk 93.81 //

children.text: sumāgadhāyāḥ kuśalānubandhaṃ puṇyaṃ prabhāvaṃ vipulaṃ vilokya /
children.translated_text: Seeing the vast merit, power, and connection with wholesome deeds of <s>Sumāgadhā</s>,

children.text: te bhikṣavas tatra kutūhalena papracchū ramyaṃ jinam ādivṛttam // KAvk_93.82 //
children.translated_text: the monks there, with curiosity, asked the Conqueror about her delightful past story. // KAvk 93.82 //

children.text: pṛṣṭaḥ sa taiḥ saṃsadi sarvadarśī sumāgadhāyāḥ kuśalasya hetum /
children.translated_text: Asked by them in the assembly, the all-seeing one, concerning the cause of <s>Sumāgadhā</s>'s merit,

children.text: dantaprabhābhiḥ kakubhāṃ mukheṣu diśan prakāśam bhagavān babhāṣe // KAvk_93.83 //
children.translated_text: shedding light upon the faces of the directions with the radiance of his teeth, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke: // KAvk 93.83 //

children.text: vārāṇasyām abhūt pūrvaṃ kṛkeḥ kantasya bhūpateḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In <s>Vārāṇasī</s> (Benares), there was formerly a daughter of King <s>Kṛkekanta</s>,
named <s>Kāñcanamālā</s>, wearing a golden necklace upon her breasts.' // KAvk 93.84 //
'She, always full of devotion to the Teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s>,

children.text: paricaryāṃ vyadhāt sārdhaṃ sakhīnāṃ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ // KAvk_93.85 //
children.translated_text: rendered service together with five hundred companions.' // KAvk 93.85 //
'Once, that king, upon seeing an ominous dream,
agitated by fear and doubt, asked those skilled in interpreting results.' // KAvk 93.86 //
'Those dream-interpreters, out of hatred for the princess, spoke:

children.text: atipriyasya hṛdayaṃ hutvāgnau labhyate śivam // KAvk_93.87 //
children.translated_text: "By offering the heart of one most dear in the fire, auspiciousness will be attained."' // KAvk 93.87 //

children.text: iti teṣām anādṛtya vacaḥ krūrataraṃ nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Disregarding the exceedingly cruel words of those [interpreters], the king

children.text: bhagavantaṃ yayau draṣṭuṃ kāśyapaṃ duhitur girā // KAvk_93.88 //
children.translated_text: went to see the <s>Bhagavān Kāśyapa</s>, at his daughter's urging.' // KAvk 93.88 //

children.text: sa tam etyāvadat svapnaḥ savikāraḥ paraṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: 'Having approached him, he said: "An ominous dream was seen by me today;

children.text: dṛṣṭo 'dya sarvaṃ sarvajña tatphalaṃ vaktum arhasi // KAvk_93.89 //
children.translated_text: O All-Knowing One, you should tell the full meaning of its result."' // KAvk 93.89 //
'"An elephant going out through a window, its tail caught;

children.text: tṛṣitasya tathā paścāt kupo dhāvan vilokitaḥ // KAvk_93.90 //
children.translated_text: and afterward, a well was seen running behind one who was thirsty."' // KAvk 93.90 //
'"One satisfied by a measure of flour selling a measure of pearls;

children.text: samīkṛtāni dṛṣṭāni kudārūṇi ca candanaiḥ // KAvk_93.9l //
children.translated_text: and inferior wood seen equated with sandalwood."' // KAvk 93.91 //
'"A great elephant summoned in battle by a young elephant;

children.text: parān aśuciliptāṅgaḥ pralimpan viplutaḥ kapiḥ // KAvk_93.92 //
children.translated_text: and a monkey, its body smeared with filth, smearing others, fallen from grace."' // KAvk 93.92 //
'"A monkey, a treasury of mischief, anointed as king of a prosperous realm;

children.text: paṭo 'ṣṭādaśabhiḥ kṛṣṭaḥ puruṣair apy asaṃkṣayaḥ // KAvk_93.93 //
children.translated_text: and a cloth pulled by eighteen men, yet inexhaustible."' // KAvk 93.93 //
'"A beautiful garden of flowers and fruits plundered by thieves;
and a great crowd of people devoted to hatred, mockery, and quarrel."' // KAvk 93.94 //
'"I think the results of these wondrous dreams are most terrible."

children.text: iti pṛṣṭaḥ kṣitibhujā bhagavān kāśyapo 'bravīt // KAvk_93.95 //
children.translated_text: Thus asked by the king, the <s>Bhagavān Kāśyapa</s> spoke:' // KAvk 93.95 //

children.text: śatāyuṣi jane śāstā śāntaḥ śākyamunir jinaḥ /
children.translated_text: '"When the lifespan of people is a hundred years, the Teacher, the peaceful Conqueror <s>Śākyamuni</s>,

children.text: bhaviṣyaty amṛtāmbhodhiḥ sa drṣṭaḥ kuñjaras tvayā // KAvk_93.96 //
children.translated_text: will arise — an ocean of the deathless. The elephant was seen by you as him."' // KAvk 93.96 //
'"In his later age too, the disciples, due to the influence of <s>Kali</s> (the age of discord),
having abandoned moral conduct, virtues, and proper behavior, will become corrupted."' // KAvk 93.97 //
'"Those immature and of little discernment will, by force upon the householders,

children.text: svayaṃ sevāṃ samālambya kariṣyanty eva deśanām // KAvk_93.98 //
children.translated_text: themselves undertaking service, give teachings [for material gain]."' // KAvk 93.98 //
'"Since that which should be sought runs in pursuit of supplicants for service,

children.text: tṛṣitasya vrajan paścāt kūpas tasmād vilokitaḥ // KAvk_93.99 //
children.translated_text: the well was seen running behind the thirsty one."' // KAvk 93.99 //
'"Those, blinded by greed, afflicted by delusion, will to others —"'
a <s>prastha</s> (measure) of pearls of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) for a <s>prastha</s> of barley-flour. (Verse 100)
The bad logs of the words of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heretical teachers), with the sandalwood of the <s>Buddha's</s> teachings —

children.text: sāmyam āpādayiṣyanti te maugdhyād aviśeṣiṇaḥ // KAvk_93.101 //
children.translated_text: those undiscriminating fools will, through their stupidity, equate them. (Verse 101)
Somewhere, having encountered a virtuous, well-trained elephant among monks,

children.text: duḥśīlakalabho bhikṣuḥ spardhayā dhik kariṣyati // KAvk_93.102 //
children.translated_text: a monk who is a young elephant of bad conduct will, out of rivalry, scorn him. (Verse 102)
A monkey-monk, with limbs smeared with fickleness and impurity,
smearing the virtuous monks with his own faults, will make them seem like himself. (Verse 103)
And the consecration of a eunuch will take place, as it were, like that of a monkey;
yet the banner of the Perfectly Awakened One's teaching, though pulled at, will not perish. (Verse 104)
Even in the orchards that are the fruits of <s>saṃgha</s> (monastic community) property, they will resort to thievery,

children.text: mithaḥ kalahaśīlāś ca bhaviṣyanty apavādinaḥ // KAvk_93.105 //
children.translated_text: and they will be quarrelsome with one another and slanderous. (Verse 105)
These are the fruits on earth at the end of the ripening of your dream.' —

children.text: iti śāstur vacaḥ śrutvā vismito 'bhūn mahīpatiḥ // KAvk_93.106 //
children.translated_text: hearing this speech of the Teacher, the king was astonished. (Verse 106)
Then, to the king together with his retinue, the Teacher, having given a <s>Dharma</s> teaching,
indicated the worthiness of merit through a garland of gold. (Verse 107)
At the end of a [previous] life, she had worshipped a <s>stūpa</s> with a garland of oranges;

children.text: sā tena sukṛtenaiva jātā hemasrajāṅkitā // KAvk_93.108 //
children.translated_text: by that very good deed, she was born marked with a golden garland. (Verse 108)
This <s>Sumāgadhā</s>, by the power of her great merit,
has now attained the state of being a bridge of virtue for the community of relatives. (Verse 109)
Having thus declared, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), through the sky, together with the monks,

children.text: rucā saṃpūrayann āśāṃ yayau jetavanaṃ jinaḥ // KAvk_93.ll0 //
children.translated_text: filling the directions with his radiance, the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) went to <s>Jetavana</s>. (Verse 110)
The strong desire for a son, for the continuity of a good family among men, is indeed in vain —

children.text: sūnuś ced aguṇas tad eva viphalaṃ tat kiṃ na sarvaṃ kulam /
children.translated_text: if the son is without virtues, then all of that is fruitless; what then of the entire family?

children.text: sā kanyā kila jāyate guṇavatī puṇyaprabhāvād yayā
children.translated_text: That daughter, indeed, is born endowed with virtues, by the power of merit, through whom

children.text: saṃsārorusaritpatau kulayugam nāv eva saṃtāryate // KAvk_93.111 //
children.translated_text: the pair of families is ferried across the great river of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) as if by a boat. (Verse 111)

body.text: iti kṣemendraviracitāyāṃ bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatāyāṃ sumāgadhāvadānaṃ trinavatitamaḥ pallavah.
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā</s> composed by <s>Kṣemendra</s>, the <s>Sumāgadhāvadāna</s> is the ninety-third branch.
